import json, os
W = '/Users/kristinarash/Library/Caches/sportsci-batch-96'

def load(i):
    return json.load(open(f'{W}/drafts/{i}.json', encoding='utf-8'))

def save(i, d, status, changes, resid, prio):
    d['verification'] = {"status": status, "changes": changes,
                         "residualConcerns": resid, "spotCheckPriority": prio}
    s = json.dumps(d, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
    assert '—' not in s, i
    open(f'{W}/verified/{i}.json', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s + '\n')

SR_NOTE = ("studyDesign kept as Systematic Review / Meta-analysis under the INSTRUCTIONS rule that Narrative Review is used only when no search method is described; "
           "the authors describe a database search but call the work a {} review and did not follow PRISMA, so a human may prefer Narrative Review.")

# Q89
d = load('Q89')
save('Q89', d, 'VERIFIED', [], '', 'normal')

# Q90
d = load('Q90'); p = d['paper']
d['screeningLimitations'] = ("The authors state the search was not run to PRISMA or scoping-review standards, and no formal appraisal of study quality is reported, although two authors screened records independently. "
    "The cited studies are mostly observational cohorts with varying definitions of successful return, and the recommendations are the authors' synthesis rather than tested interventions.")
p['findings'] = p['findings'].replace(
    "Only 17% of athletes after ACLR met a 90% between-limb symmetry standard on a return-to-sport test battery",
    "Only 17% of athletes after ACLR, and 24% of non-injured athletes, met a 90% between-limb symmetry standard on a return-to-sport test battery")
p['methods'] = ("A practical review of 158 unique articles found in Google Scholar, Medline and SPORTDiscus (June to November 2023), with at least two authors screening titles, abstracts and full texts and with reference checking. "
    "The search was not conducted to PRISMA or scoping-review standards, and each author was assigned writing sections based on clinical expertise.")
p['limitations'] = ("The review has no formal risk-of-bias appraisal and was not conducted to PRISMA or scoping-review standards. "
    "Most included evidence comes from retrospective or registry cohorts, outcome definitions differ across studies, and several medical recommendations rest on expert judgement rather than direct comparative trials.")
save('Q90', d, 'CORRECTED', [
    "screeningLimitations: said selection was 'not systematic or reproducible' -> search terms, databases and dates are printed and 'at least two authors were involved in independently screening'; now says not PRISMA-standard and no formal appraisal",
    "paper.limitations: 'search strategy is not reproducible' -> removed; search is 'not in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines or that of a scoping review'",
    "paper.methods: 'narrative review' wording and missing dual screening -> added independent screening by at least two authors",
    "paper.findings: added the non-injured comparison ('17 % of athletes after ACLR and 24 % of non-injured athletes demonstrating symmetric performance')"],
    SR_NOTE.format("practical") + " Clinically relevant to ACL return-to-sport clearance.", 'high')

# Q91
d = load('Q91'); p = d['paper']
p['findings'] = p['findings'].replace(
    "MLB pitchers' fastball velocity fell by 1.3% (P = .004) and pitch count fell by 60.7% in season 1 (P = .007), with both recovering by seasons 2 and 3.",
    "MLB pitchers who had surgery on their lead leg showed a 1.3% fall in fastball velocity (P = .004) and a 60.7% fall in pitch count in season 1 (P = .007), with both recovering by seasons 2 and 3.")
p['citation'] = "Schallmo MS, Fitzpatrick TH, Yancey HB, Marquez-Lara A, Luo TD, Stubbs AJ. Return-to-Play and Performance Outcomes of Professional Athletes in North America After Hip Arthroscopy From 1999 to 2016. Am J Sports Med. 2018:1-11."
save('Q91', d, 'CORRECTED', [
    "paper.findings: pitch velocity and pitch count changes attributed to all MLB pitchers -> lead-leg pitchers only ('MLB pitchers who underwent surgery specifically on their lead leg ... (-60.7%, P = .007)')",
    "paper.citation: 'pp. 1-11' formatting -> '2018:1-11' (online-first pagination as printed; volume placeholder 'Vol. XX' omitted)"],
    "Hip arthroscopy return-to-play in professional athletes; return-time figures should not be read as clearance criteria.", 'high')

# Q92
d = load('Q92')
save('Q92', d, 'VERIFIED', [], '', 'normal')

# Q93
d = load('Q93'); p = d['paper']
d['screeningLimitations'] = ("The study has no return-to-play dates, reinjury or performance outcomes, clubs used their own rehabilitation protocols, and only players who met functional criteria for return in the first year were included. "
    "The authors note thermal camera accuracy is normally about +/-2 degrees C, and no temperature value was tested against any return outcome.")
p['limitations'] = ("The study has no return-to-play dates or reinjury outcomes, and no other rehabilitation or performance measures were collected. "
    "Clubs used different rehabilitation protocols, leagues were heterogeneous, and only players who met functional criteria in the first year were included. "
    "The abstract states both predictors were significant, but Table 2 shows sex was not (P = 0.18).")
p['practicalImplications'] = ("Staff can track the injured minus healthy knee temperature asymmetry at set time points after ACL reconstruction, and look for a steady decline over the first year. "
    "A single asymmetry value should not be read as a clearance threshold, and combining knee with thigh temperature asymmetry is only proposed by the authors as future research.")
d['paper']['athleteDev'] = ("Thermography could give performance staff an extra monitoring point in the year after ACL reconstruction, where the study shows a gradual decline in knee asymmetry that was still above healthy-knee values at day 365. "
    "It should sit alongside strength, hop and load data rather than replace them.")
save('Q93', d, 'CORRECTED', [
    "screeningLimitations: 'the authors say the data cannot yet support fixed pass or fail thresholds' -> removed, not stated in text (authors instead claim the study 'established a Tsk progression criterion')",
    "paper.limitations: added abstract vs table conflict ('both predictor variables were significant' vs Table 2 'Gender 0.14 ... 0.18')",
    "paper.practicalImplications: presented thigh temperature and strength balance as an author recommendation -> it is a future research line ('can be combined with those of the front and back thigh Tsk. This study did not include these values')",
    "paper.athleteDev: 'around day 35 to 187 when the study shows the asymmetry trend' -> unsupported; the decline runs through the year and the authors note possibly 'no significant change ... between days 35 and 63'"],
    "Authors frame thermography as a return-to-play criterion without any outcome validation; record now says this explicitly. Model intercept (1.92) and the authors' stated day-0 estimate (2.52 degrees C) do not reconcile in the text; both are reported as printed.", 'high')

# Q94
d = load('Q94')
save('Q94', d, 'VERIFIED', [], '', 'normal')

# Q95 / Q96 shared corrections
def wada(i, dup):
    d = load(i); p = d['paper']
    d['evidenceSummary'] = ("A review of PubMed-identified studies and reviews of the 23 substance classes on the 2018 WADA Prohibited List, using double-blind randomized trials in trained subjects as the main evidence standard. "
        "The authors report that 5 classes (anabolic agents, beta2-agonists, stimulants, glucocorticoids and beta-blockers) show evidence of enhancing actual sports performance, mainly strength or sprint performance, and growth hormone has similar evidence only in untrained subjects. "
        "The level 1 evidence base is 11 studies with 266 subjects, and the authors found no studies showing benefit on reliable markers of endurance performance.")
    d['synthesisCaution'] = ("Staff could read the finding that most classes lack evidence as proof that the substances do not improve performance, when 11 classes simply have no well-designed studies and only 6 classes have evidence of no effect.")
    p['tldr'] = ("Most of the substances on the WADA Prohibited List have no convincing evidence of improving athletic performance in trained athletes. "
        "The few classes with evidence improve strength, sprint or accuracy tasks, and the authors found no studies showing benefit on reliable markers of endurance performance.")
    p['findings'] = ("Five classes showed evidence of enhancing actual performance in trained subjects: anabolic agents (strength, three studies with 91 volunteers), beta2-agonists (peak sprint power and muscle strength, three studies with 39 volunteers), "
        "stimulants (muscle strength, sprint performance and 1500 m run time, 58 trained subjects in Table 1), glucocorticoids (one study with 10 subjects, 11% gain in one-legged hopping force, a surrogate marker) and beta-blockers (13.4% better shooting, one study of 33 subjects). "
        "Growth hormone improved sprint performance in untrained subjects only, 11 classes had no well-designed studies, and 6 classes had evidence of no relevant effect.")
    p['limitations'] = ("The search used PubMed only with keyword combinations, and no formal appraisal or PRISMA reporting is described. "
        "The authors note that trials of banned substances in elite athletes are very hard or impossible to run, so the target population is largely missing, and that endurance surrogates such as VO2max have limited predictive value for performance.")
    changes = [
        "paper.findings: stimulants described as 'two studies in the text that the authors describe as mixed' -> not in text; Table 1 lists 'Muscle strength, sprint performance, 1500 m run time Total: 58'",
        "paper.findings: '11 of 23 classes had no well-designed studies in trained subjects' -> 'For 11 classes, no well-designed studies are available'; added 'for the remaining six classes, there is evidence of an absence of a positive effect'",
        "paper.limitations: attributed PubMed-only search and other points to the authors as stated limitations -> no limitations section exists; now reviewer-stated search limits plus authors' points on elite populations ('very challenging, or even impossible') and VO2max",
        "synthesisCaution: added that 6 classes do have evidence of no effect"]
    if i == 'Q95':
        changes.append("evidenceSummary/tldr: 'no class showed a benefit on endurance performance' -> 'no studies showing positive effects on reliable markers of endurance performance' (EPO raised VO2max and time to exhaustion)")
    else:
        changes.append("paper.tldr: 'none improve endurance performance' -> 'no studies showing positive effects on reliable markers of endurance performance' (EPO raised VO2max and time to exhaustion)")
    save(i, d, 'CORRECTED', changes,
         f"Duplicate of {dup}: same article and DOI (10.1007/s40279-018-1014-1); keep one record. " + SR_NOTE.format("narrative-style") +
         (" This copy is the online-first version (no volume or pages printed, year 2018); Q96 prints Sports Medicine (2019) 49:525-539." if i == 'Q95' else " This copy prints the issue citation (2019) 49:525-539; Q95 is the online-first copy."),
         'high')

wada('Q95', 'Q96')
wada('Q96', 'Q95')
print('ok')
